memory_update.text: The purest high-end BaTiO3 dielectric-powder suppliers for AI-server MLCCs appear to be non-US listed or private; US-listed exposure is mostly downstream MLCC makers, OTC ADRs, or adjacent passive-component suppliers.

Sakai Chemical 4078.JP should remain the key non-US upstream reference for future non-US universe expansion, but it should not be inserted into a US-listed candidate list unless a verifiable US-traded ordinary/ADR instrument is found.

For US-listed candidates, the correct falsification test is not simply MLCC exposure; it is evidence of high-capacitance/thin-layer MLCC demand, AI-server qualification, pricing power, capacity tightness, or dielectric-powder procurement constraints.

Vishay is the best-fit US-listed underfollowed candidate found in this pass, but its direct link to AI-server-grade thin-layer MLCCs and sub-100nm BaTiO3 powder is weak and must be treated as a hypothesis until product mix and customer exposure are verified.

node: AI server MLCC upstream dielectric powders
summary: Layer 1B found that the purest upstream dielectric-powder exposure appears difficult to express through US-listed common equities: the strongest named merchant-powder lead is Sakai Chemical in Japan, while Ferro/Vibrantz is private and other powder suppliers are non-US or weakly mapped. For US-listed instruments, the actionable universe is mostly downstream or adjacent: OTC ADRs of Japanese MLCC leaders and one US-listed passive-component supplier. The underfollowed lane therefore should not overstate direct BaTiO3 powder exposure; it should track whether AI-server MLCC tightness flows into pricing, mix, capacity, or material procurement commentary at MLCC makers and adjacent capacitor suppliers.
